thread:
chris: hey @sabrina — customer reported streaming cutoff on long gen when behind corp proxy. SDK v0.14.2. They set REDWOOD_TIMEOUT env var and also passed timeout=(5,120) to Client; unclear which wins.
sabrina: is this the connect vs read vs total confusion? usually a socket read timeout during long completion causes mid-stream stop.
chris: i got a quick repro from them, sharing snippet below. they do stream=True and the stream abruptly stops after ~30s of tokens.
```python
from redwood import Client
client = Client(api_key="REDACTED", timeout=(5, 120))  # (connect, read) style they used
resp = client.generate(model="redwood-v0", prompt="<long prompt>", stream=True, max_tokens=1024)
for chunk in resp:
    print(chunk.text, end="")
```
devon: FYI httpx timeout semantics: it accepts (connect, read) tuple or httpx.Timeout object. our Python SDK wraps httpx but historically accepted a two-item tuple. env vars like REDWOOD_TIMEOUT_MS were added later — could be a ms vs s mismatch. which env names did they set?
chris: they had REDWOOD_TIMEOUT=120 and REDWOOD_TIMEOUT_MS=120000 in different services (messy). also they're behind a corp nginx that has proxy_read_timeout 30s.
sabrina: nginx proxy_read_timeout = 30s will kill the upstream stream regardless of client timeout. have them check nginx conf, and run a direct test to our endpoint (bypass proxy) using curl to confirm.
ops-jen: i've seen exactly this with ALB/nginx keeping an idle read timeout — it looks like SDK cutoff. ask customer to run: 
```bash
curl -v --no-buffer -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -d @payload.json
```
if the connection drops at ~30s, upstream is the culprit.
devon: also streaming chunk cutoff can happen if the SDK enforces a total deadline (e.g., interpreting a single numeric timeout as a total). if they passed tuple but our arg parsing coerced it, they might be hitting total_deadline. request pip freeze to confirm sdk==0.14.2.
chris: i've asked for full pip freeze and httpx version. asked them to re-run with env REDWOOD_DEBUG_HTTPX=1 to collect httpx debug logs.
support-bot: Ticket SUP-7234 created; priority P2; assigned to eng-runtime.
sabrina: immediate triage steps to send customer: 1) bypass corp proxy (curl direct). 2) run with client timeout=None or a higher total timeout. 3) set REDWOOD_DEBUG_HTTPX=1 and share logs. 4) try smaller max_tokens to see if generation completes. 5) share nginx/ALB idle timeout settings.
devon: long-term: we should clarify docs about tuple vs single value vs env var precedence, and consider deprecating ambiguous tuple parsing. also think about retry behavior for streaming (we can't easily restart partial streams).
chris: thanks — i'll update the ticket with these repro steps and ask for network traces. adding note about ms vs s env var confusion. :thumbsup:
ops-jen: pinging eng-runtime for visibility — this surfaces regularly with corporate proxies.
